title: Only 11% Can Pass This Firefighter Entrance Exam
summary: Explore fire science and incident reasoning through clues, practical situations and fresh challenges.

landing.intro:
Read the clues. Make the connections.
Put your thinking to the test.

about.body: Connect the facts, notice the details and test your understanding of fire science and incident reasoning. Each checkpoint reveals your topic profile before a different challenge begins.

steps: Read the clues and choose one answer.
See your topic profile at each checkpoint and continue to a new challenge.
Reveal your overall result, then optionally review the answers you missed.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an accredited firefighter entrance exam, employment assessment, fitness test, qualification, operational training course or source of emergency advice. Fire-service procedures vary worldwide; always follow local emergency services and qualified professional guidance.

firefighter-s1q1.question: Which three elements are commonly represented by the fire triangle?

firefighter-s1q2.question: What is fuel in the context of a fire?

firefighter-s1q3.question: What can removing a necessary element of the fire triangle do?

firefighter-s1q4.question: Why is smoke a serious hazard?

answers.a2: It can contain toxic gases and particles and reduce visibility
answers.a4: It is always harmless when pale

answers.a1: Heat transfer through direct contact within or between materials
answers.a3: Heat transfer only by moving air

answers.a2: Heat transfer through the movement of a fluid such as air
answers.a3: Heat transfer only through solid metal

answers.a2: Heat that needs direct contact at all times
answers.a4: Heat carried only by a water hose

firefighter-s2q1.question: Why can poor visibility make movement through a smoke-filled area dangerous?

answers.a1: Obstacles, exits and changes in layout may be difficult to identify
answers.a3: Visibility has no effect on orientation
answers.a4: Every exit becomes easier to see

firefighter-s2q2.question: A room has no visible flames but contains smoke. What is the sound conclusion?

answers.a1: There can be no toxic gases
answers.a2: The absence of visible flames does not establish safety

firefighter-s2q3.question: Why can hot gases collect near a ceiling?

answers.a2: Heated gases tend to rise relative to cooler surrounding air

firefighter-s2q4.question: What does a smoke alarm primarily provide?

answers.a1: A guarantee that every person has escaped
answers.a2: An early warning that smoke may be present
answers.a4: Proof of the exact fire location

firefighter-s2q5.question: Why should a closed door not be assumed to make a nearby fire irrelevant?

answers.a1: Smoke cannot move through any gap
answers.a3: A closed door proves the fire is out
answers.a4: Heat and smoke conditions can still change and spread

firefighter-s2q6.question: What makes carbon monoxide particularly difficult for people to notice without detection equipment?

answers.a3: It always has a bright red colour
answers.a4: It always smells strongly of smoke

firefighter-s2q7.question: Why do firefighters use appropriate respiratory protection in hazardous atmospheres?

answers.a2: Breathing hazards occur only after flames disappear
answers.a3: Ordinary air may contain dangerous contaminants or insufficient oxygen
answers.a4: Cloth masks provide the same protection in every atmosphere

firefighter-s3q1.question: At an unfamiliar incident, what is the purpose of an initial scene assessment?

answers.a4: Identify hazards and guide a coordinated response

firefighter-s3q2.question: A damaged electrical cable is near water. What should responders recognise?

answers.a1: A potential electrical hazard requiring the appropriate procedure
answers.a2: A reason to touch it to test for current
answers.a3: A guarantee that water removes the hazard
answers.a4: Proof that the cable is safe

firefighter-s3q3.question: Why keep an escape route under consideration during an operation?

answers.a1: A route can never become obstructed
answers.a2: It proves the structure is stable
answers.a3: Conditions may change and require withdrawal

firefighter-s3q4.question: A container holds an unknown chemical. What is the appropriate approach?

answers.a2: Mix it with another substance to see what happens
answers.a3: Use identification and hazardous-material procedures rather than guessing
answers.a4: Assume every clear liquid is water

firefighter-s3q5.question: Why can a visibly damaged structure require specialist assessment?

answers.a3: A photograph proves it cannot collapse

firefighter-s3q6.question: At a road incident, what additional hazard may need control?

answers.a1: Only the age of the vehicles
answers.a2: Only the colour of road signs
answers.a4: Only the number of photographs taken

firefighter-s3q7.question: Why should an operational plan change when hazards change?

answers.a1: The original assumptions may no longer be valid
answers.a2: New hazards automatically solve old ones
answers.a4: Plans are never allowed to use new information

firefighter-s4q1.question: What is the purpose of inspecting equipment before use?

answers.a1: To identify defects and confirm suitability
answers.a4: To guarantee it can never fail

firefighter-s4q2.question: A hose has visible damage. What should happen?

answers.a1: Ignore it if the colour is unchanged
answers.a2: Hide the damage under tape and assume it is sound
answers.a3: Use it at higher pressure to test it informally
answers.a4: Follow the inspection and removal-from-service procedure

firefighter-s4q3.question: Why must a ladder be used according to its rated capacity and instructions?

answers.a3: Its stability and strength have limits
answers.a4: Instructions apply only to new ladders

firefighter-s4q4.question: What is a pump’s basic purpose?

answers.a2: To move a fluid by supplying energy
answers.a3: To turn every liquid into fuel

firefighter-s4q5.question: Why can a pressurised line create a movement hazard?

answers.a2: Forces can act on the line and its connections
answers.a3: Only an empty line can move

firefighter-s4q6.question: A tool has a guard. What is the guard generally intended to do?

answers.a4: Reduce contact with a hazard during intended use

firefighter-s4q7.question: Why should damaged protective clothing be reported?

answers.a3: Its protective performance may be compromised

answers.a1: The temperature at which water freezes
answers.a4: A force that opposes relative motion between contacting surfaces

firefighter-s5q2.question: What does a lever turn around?

firefighter-s5q3.question: Two meshed external gears turn together. If one turns clockwise, how does the other turn?

firefighter-s5q4.question: What does a pulley change in a simple fixed-pulley system?

answers.a3: The direction of the applied force

firefighter-s5q6.question: What does a spring generally do when compressed within its elastic range?

answers.a2: Stores energy and tends to return to its original shape

firefighter-s5q7.question: Why can lubrication reduce wear between moving parts?

answers.a3: It makes all parts the same size

firefighter-s6q1.question: A plan shows north at the top. A room is directly right of the entrance. In which direction is it?

firefighter-s6q2.question: A person faces west and turns 90° to the right. Which direction do they face?

firefighter-s6q3.question: A rectangular floor is 6 m long and 4 m wide. What is its area?

firefighter-s6q4.question: Three sections of hose are 15 m, 20 m and 25 m long. What is their combined length?

firefighter-s6q5.question: A corridor has doors at 5 m intervals. The first door is at 5 m. Where is the fourth door?

firefighter-s6q6.question: A team travels 30 m north, then 10 m south. Where is it relative to the start?

firefighter-s6q7.question: On a diagram, a valve is between a tank and a pump. What is the order from the tank?

firefighter-s7q1.question: A supply box holds 24 items. Six are used. What fraction remains?

firefighter-s7q2.question: A task begins at 14:35 and lasts 50 minutes. When does it finish?

firefighter-s7q3.question: Four equal groups share 36 items. How many items are in each group?

firefighter-s7q4.question: A reading rises from 40 to 50. What is the percentage increase?

firefighter-s7q5.question: A plan uses a scale of 1 cm to 2 m. What distance does 6 cm represent?

firefighter-s7q6.question: Three loads weigh 12 kg, 15 kg and 18 kg. What is their total mass?

firefighter-s7q7.question: A checklist has 20 items. Four remain unchecked. What percentage is complete?

firefighter-s8q1.question: An important instruction is unclear. What is the best response?

firefighter-s8q2.question: What is the purpose of reading back a critical instruction?

answers.a1: To make the message longer for its own sake
answers.a2: To let the sender check that it was understood correctly
answers.a3: To replace carrying out the confirmed instruction
answers.a4: To transfer all responsibility to the sender

firefighter-s8q3.question: Two tasks require the same person at the same time. What should be clarified?

answers.a2: Only the colour of the checklist
answers.a3: Which task has the shorter name

answers.a1: Relevant facts, unresolved concerns and the next required actions
answers.a2: Only a reassurance that everything is fine

firefighter-s8q5.question: A colleague reports a new safety concern. What supports effective teamwork?

answers.a2: Hide it to protect the schedule
answers.a3: Dismiss it because the colleague is junior
answers.a4: Listen, clarify and address the concern

firefighter-s8q6.question: A procedure changes. Which document should guide the task?

answers.a2: Any older copy that looks familiar
answers.a4: A remembered version from another organisation

firefighter-s8q7.question: Why assign a clear owner to a follow-up action?

answers.a1: So responsibility and completion can be tracked
answers.a3: So nobody else may raise concerns
answers.a4: So the action becomes automatically complete

firefighter-s9q1.question: Two people give different times for the same event. What is the best next step?

answers.a2: Choose the more confident speaker automatically
answers.a3: Average the times and call that a fact
answers.a4: Check each account against other reliable information

firefighter-s9q2.question: Which statement records an observation rather than an assumption about motive?

answers.a1: The person left because they were guilty
answers.a2: The person intended to mislead everyone
answers.a3: The person never cared about the meeting
answers.a4: The person left the room at 14:10

firefighter-s9q3.question: A photograph has no known date or location. What should be checked before relying on it?

answers.a4: Whether it matches a preferred conclusion

firefighter-s9q4.question: A claim is repeated by three websites, all quoting one unnamed source. What does that show?

answers.a1: Repeated reporting, not three independent confirmations
answers.a2: Proof that the claim is accurate
answers.a3: Proof that no further checking is needed

firefighter-s9q5.question: All authorised visitors have a pass. Mira has a pass. What follows from that rule alone?

answers.a1: It does not prove Mira is an authorised visitor
answers.a3: Mira must be an authorised visitor
answers.a4: Mira cannot be an authorised visitor

firefighter-s9q6.question: A new reliable fact contradicts your initial explanation. What is the sound response?

answers.a1: Change the fact to fit the explanation
answers.a2: Treat your first idea as unchangeable

firefighter-s9q7.question: A report says an event happened after a change. Does that timing alone prove the change caused it?

answers.a1: Yes; if the report is long enough
answers.a4: No; earlier events can never cause later ones

firefighter-s10q1.question: A team member has not acknowledged an important message. What needs to be confirmed?

answers.a2: That the action is already complete
answers.a3: Whether the message was received and understood
answers.a4: Only whether the sender spoke loudly

firefighter-s10q2.question: A crew notices a new hazard outside its immediate task. What supports safety?

answers.a1: Assume the original plan covers every change
answers.a2: Ignore it because another crew may notice
answers.a3: Communicate it promptly through the incident structure
answers.a4: Keep it private until the operation ends

firefighter-s10q3.question: Why account for personnel during an incident?

answers.a2: To know who is deployed and whether anyone is missing
answers.a3: To determine the cause of the fire

firefighter-s10q4.question: A task exceeds a tool’s stated capability. What is appropriate?

answers.a1: Let the schedule decide the capacity
answers.a2: Use a suitable authorised method or equipment
answers.a4: Assume extra effort removes the limit

firefighter-s10q5.question: Two instructions conflict. What should be resolved?

answers.a1: Which person spoke last regardless of role
answers.a2: Nothing; both can always happen simultaneously
answers.a4: The intended priority and authorised direction

firefighter-s10q6.question: Why is a post-incident review useful?

answers.a1: It identifies lessons and improvements from what happened
answers.a3: It proves every initial assumption was right
answers.a4: It guarantees the next incident will be identical

firefighter-s10q7.question: Which report is most useful to an incident coordinator?

answers.a2: An unverified cause presented as certain
answers.a3: Only the reporter’s opinion of another team
answers.a4: A clear location, observed hazard and relevant change
